title: IncidentPilot - SLOs and the AI feature
description: The platform's own SLIs, and the governance panels for the AI feature. Most people build an SRE tool and never define its SLIs; this is the dashboard that says otherwise.

panels.title: Citation coverage (must read 1.0)
panels.description: A FLAT LINE AT 1.0 IS THE POINT. Grounding has a zero error budget because it is an invariant enforced by a deterministic validator, not a probabilistic target. NaN before the first PIR is deliberate: a gauge reading 0 on a fresh pod is indistinguishable from a real violation, and would page on every deploy.

panels.title: Ingest error-budget burn rate
panels.description: Multi-window burn rate against a 99.9% objective. Two windows always: the long one says the problem is real, the short one says it is still happening.

panels.title: PIR generation by layer
panels.description: llm_primary, llm_secondary, skeleton. A run of skeletons means delivery is meeting its SLO while the feature is effectively absent, which is why EverythingIsASkeleton is its own alert.

panels.title: Validation rejections by reason
panels.description: Check the reason before blaming the model. A spike in 'unsupported' is usually the support threshold being too strict after a change, and a false rejection pushes honest drafts to the skeleton.

panels.title: Cost per PIR (budget $0.50)
panels.description: Settle a model change with the eval harness rather than a price list: replay the 40-incident corpus with --set roles.synthesize.model=<candidate>.

panels.title: Budget breaker trips
panels.description: Per incident, per day, per month. A trip degrades to the skeleton and never blocks: a cost control that can make an outage worse is a bug.

panels.title: Transcript completeness (SLO 99.99%)
panels.description: THE REAL AVAILABILITY METRIC. The bot can be 100% up and still have silently dropped three messages, after which the PIR is wrong and nobody notices. Sampled rather than counted (ADR 0003).

panels.title: conversations.history callers (reconciler only)
panels.description: INV-02 as a time series. Slack allows one call per minute workspace-wide, so a hot-path caller starves the reconciler and silently shortens every transcript.

panels.title: Human edit ratio by prompt version
panels.description: How much a human had to rewrite. Almost nobody measures this, which is exactly why it is here: it is the only panel that can make the AI feature look bad.
